caveats: A hybrid. The website HTML holds each paragraph in its own element, so unnumbered paragraphs are separate, footnotes are linked and a paragraph is never cut at a page break. Wayback holds about two thirds of its pages (chapters 4, 7, 8 and 9 are mostly missing): a stretch whose printed paragraph numbers the HTML has is taken from the HTML, the rest from the PDF's tags.

The tags put one /P element around all the paragraphs between headings on a page: split at printed paragraph numbers (2.1.60), so unnumbered paragraphs inside one element are not separated in the stretches taken from the tags.

In the tags a fragment that continues an unfinished paragraph (past the page's notes) is joined to it, whatever its first letter; footnotes sit inside the page's /P in the note size (9 pt against 12 pt) and are taken out by size.

2026-10-03 (reportsthatmatter-ivg.3): 37 more website pages fetched from Wayback (the Foreword, the Report summary, Part 1 page 2, Part 2's introduction, Part 3, the appendices, and chapter pages 3.10, 3.11a, 4.1, 6.8, 6.10, 6.16, 9.1, 10.12a, 12.10a), several only in 2012-2015 captures (later ones are 503 error pages). The served text (ingest.ts, cleanEdition) reads them. The scoring reference (blocks.jsonl, built 2026-10-02) is unchanged, so a score against it is not inflated by them; but reference.py's build lists the directory, so rebuilding it would take in the new part- and ch- pages and make reference and served text share more of their source: rebuild it only knowingly. The website edition is the report as the Panel published it online, Crown copyright under the Open Government Licence v3.0, like the PDF.
